EnergyNet
ML Ratchet · vehicle energy · v1.0

EnergyNet

The energy a trip will take, before it happens, with an error bar. Fuel for petrol cars and hybrids, battery kWh for electric cars, both for plug-ins, from cars to buses and trucks. The network never saw a real fuel log: it learned from a vehicle simulator driving real roads, and it is graded on 25,793 real trips it never saw.

Ann Arbor trips the network never saw

Vehicle Energy Dataset, 2017–18. What the network got: the car's class, powertrain, engine size, weight rounded to 500 lb, window-sticker label, logged speed, lidar grade and airport weather. Measured fuel is the OBD estimate; battery energy is logged current × voltage.

Where it fails: VED trip error by condition

Calibrating the simulator on 16 dev cars

Twin tests: simulate the dev car on its own logged trip

Each dev car was rebuilt in the simulator from what VED knows about it, then driven on its own 1,498 logged trips. The mismatch, measured stage by stage, became the calibration rungs. Fixes live in wrappers outside the frozen simulator.

    The ratchet

    Every rung, kept or not

    A rung is kept if it beats the incumbent's skill on the frozen simulated validation set (3,991 trips by 400 unseen vehicles; current physics version) by more than 0.01 and its dev error (mean of 15 real dev metrics) is not more than 1 point worse. Skill = 1 − median log error / median log error of the class-median guess.

    How it was built

    Physics first, then a network, then reality

    1. Simulator. RoadSim (Phase 1): forward vehicle model with measured EPA engine and motor maps, transmissions, batteries, HVAC, every hybrid control strategy; energy ledger closes to <0.05%. Frozen; every fix here is a wrapper.
    2. Vehicles. 2,400 training and 400 validation vehicles from the generator (all 7 classes, all 7 powertrains), widened to older, less efficient engines (dev twins needed engine efficiency factors 0.72–1.07) and articulated buses. Each light-duty vehicle got simulated window-sticker labels (FTP/HWFET plus the EPA 5-cycle formulas).
    3. Routes. 1,092 real Ann Arbor routes from 17 unlabelled cars (speed, lidar grade, airport weather), 14 EPA and heavy-duty cycles, and synthetic drives with stops, hills, heading and weather. The network sees station weather; the simulated car drives a different truth (temperature ± 1.5 °C, wind × 0.4–0.9 for car height).
    4. Spec masking. Each epoch redraws what is known: from EPA-like (exact mass, road-load A/B/C, engine, gears) down to class and powertrain only, with label noise.
    5. Network. Five MLPs (149 inputs: 90 route numbers, 12 road-load integrals, 47 vehicle fields with masks; 4 hidden layers; 204k weights each) predict a correction to a generic road-load energy estimate, a log-sigma, and five energy components.
    6. Exam. VED exam cars, EPA exam families, ZTBus, Mersin and ICCT, scored once.

    Where not to trust it

      Use it

      The release

      energynet-v1.0.zip: numpy-only inference (features, ensemble weights, dev sigma factors), a demo on real exam trips, the model card and every training script.

      from energynet import EnergyNet
net = EnergyNet()
trip = {'v': speed_mps, 'grade': grade, 'T_amb': temp_C, 'wind_speed': ws, 'wind_dir': wd, 'heading': hd}
car = {'class': 'car', 'architecture': 'hev_powersplit', 'mass_kg': 1497, 'mass_kind': 'reported',
       'displacement_L': 1.8, 'label_city': 48, 'label_hwy': 43, 'thermal': 'warm', 'obd_maf': False}
r = net.predict(trip, car)      # r['value'] g fuel, r['lo68'], r['hi68'], r['components_MJ']
      Data and credits
      • Vehicle Energy Dataset (VED): G. S. Oh, D. J. LeBlanc, H. Peng, IEEE T-ITS 2020 (Apache-2.0).
      • US EPA test-car lists 2008–2026, dynamometer schedules, ALPHA engine and motor maps; fueleconomy.gov; USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar; Iowa Environmental Mesonet ASOS weather; eCFR 40 CFR 1037 cycles (public domain / free use).
      • ZTBus: F. Widmer et al., ETH Zurich (CC-BY-4.0). Mersin route 33M bus trips: Y. Abut, Zenodo (CC-BY-4.0). ICCT 2018 tractor-trailer tests (Rodriguez, Delgado, Muncrief).
      • Part of ML Ratchet, github.com/dogum/ML-Ratchet: trained on physics, graded on reality.
